pages.text: Drip, drip, splash! Ria the river begins as a tiny trickle high up in the hills.
Gravity pulls the water downhill. Ria starts to move, winding and wiggling across the land.
More streams join in. With each splash and merge, Ria grows wider and stronger.
Ria passes through green valleys where plants grow tall and animals come to drink.
People build towns near Ria. River water helps farms grow food and people travel by boat.
Sometimes the river moves fast. Other times, Ria slows down and spreads wide across the land.
Ria carries soil and tiny rocks. Over time, rivers can change the shape of the land.
After a long journey, Ria reaches a big body of water. Many rivers end in seas or oceans.
Fresh river water mixes with salty ocean water. The journey is complete, but the water keeps moving.
At bedtime, we remember: rivers flow downhill, grow along the way, and help life across the land.
